description: Selectors, toolchain pins, reproduction commands and independent checks from which the seal tool builds the frozen input list of the final frozen-source clean Assurance. It differs from the current-completion template in the kernel replay, which is cold: every kernel session that the sealed kernel replay manifest names is rebuilt in a heap store that starts empty, from the sealed sources only, and compared with the recorded results; no recorded heap, database or proof object is read by the build. The product root is enumerated from Git; the runtime-link evidence root, the maintainer tool root, the Veri formal root and the AFP entry are enumerated only through the obligation ledger and the sealed input lists.

bundles.description: Isabelle theories, sessions and dependency locks that define the abstract model, the transaction relation and the runtime bridge constants.
Kernel schema and generated ABI, receipt schema, conformance vectors and the normative proposal and profile documents.
Final Solidity sources of the three profiles, their tests and symbolic harnesses, and the compiler configuration.
Recorded runtime identities, the release manifest, the deterministic build receipt, the runtime binding and the prepared code identity document that the Assurance compares against a fresh build.
Conditional evidence ledgers, the central closure artifacts, the prepared tail documents and the SDK that consumes the receipt format.
Verification scripts and continuous-integration workflows that the reproduction commands run.

The current runtime-link obligation ledger, the ledger that the sealed certificate locator file names; for every kernel run it cites, the recorded result, the recorded command and the session sources of every evidence directory that command loads; the input lists of the saved-mode recomputations, each naming every private file that recomputation reads; and the kernel replay kit: its manifest of the recorded chain with the recorded heap, database and fingerprint of every session, its catalog, its command template, its tools and step scripts, and every source file and session root file that a kernel replay reads, including the Veri formal sources and the AFP entry.
Every other tracked file of the product commit, so that the whole release tree is frozen.

reproduction.purpose: Compile the sealed sources with the pinned compiler.
reproduction.passCriterion: Exit code 0, and every runtime identity recomputed by the tail preparation code identity check equals the sealed code identity document.

reproduction.purpose: Run the unit, fuzz, invariant and pinned upstream integration tests of the three profiles.
reproduction.command: python3 scripts/prepare-trex-integration.py && FOUNDRY_FUZZ_RUNS=256 FOUNDRY_INVARIANT_RUNS=256 FOUNDRY_INVARIANT_DEPTH=500 forge test -vv
reproduction.passCriterion: Exit code 0 with no skipped suite.

reproduction.purpose: Recompute every prepared tail document from the sealed sources and compiled artifacts.
reproduction.passCriterion: Exit code 0: every generated document is byte-identical to its sealed copy.

reproduction.purpose: Run the conditional evidence verifiers of the product.

Rehash the private certificate registry and its locator file, rebuild the registry in closure mode from the sealed evidence with the sealed tool, and compare it with the sealed registry and its public record. The registry, the locator file and every evidence file the rebuild reads are frozen by the sealed input list of this recomputation. No prover or kernel session is rerun.

Rehash the private route disposition test receipt, its forge report, the malformed probe receipt and the stored route inventory, recompute the test receipt from the forge report, rebuild the inventory in closure mode with the sealed tool and compare it with the stored inventory and its public record. Foundry is not rerun.

Rehash the private typed failure probe, mutant, frozen build and load scan records and the seven compiled artifacts, recompute every probe and mutant receipt from its forge report and the load scan from the compiled artifacts, and compare them with the stored records and the public record. Neither Foundry nor the compiler is rerun.

Rehash the private call frame report and the stored proof graphs, node files, boundary records and node inventories of the 42 registered requests outside canonical form, recompute the report with the sealed tool and compare it with the stored report and the public record. The stage index, the report and every evidence file the recomputation reads are frozen by the sealed input list of this recomputation. No prover, symbolic execution or kernel session is rerun.

Rehash the stored build information and the private reflection scan report, rerun the sealed scan tool on the stored build information against the sealed product tree and compare the result with the stored report and the public record. The compiler is not rerun.

Rehash the completed kernel session databases and the stored build information, reread every reader source from the session database that stored it, recompute the read forms, the comparison with the crosswalk, the recorded-world theorems, the cell theorem statements and the compiled struct member locations, and compare them with the public record. No prover or compiler runs The private index and every file it names are frozen by the sealed input list of this recomputation.

Rehash the completed kernel session databases, the result, input snapshots and build log of every kernel run and the private certificate registry, reread every quoted definition and theorem from the session database that stored it with its text and context, reread the kernel markers and final audits, follow the parent heap of every session, rehash every input file that each run recorded at its recorded location, and compare the derived record with the public record. The private index, every file it names and every run input at its recorded location are frozen by the sealed input list of this recomputation. No prover runs.

Rehash the private word guard probe receipts of the unmodified copy and of every declared bounded word guard mutant, compare each receipt with the public record and check that the recorded inputs are the sealed catalog, mutant list, runners and probe sources. Foundry is not rerun.

Check the registered central closure record and its positive, negative and compiled-consumer records against the sealed product tree: every cited record is current and passes the evidence contract of the policy check, every acceptance criterion is quoted from the sealed conditions list and every named field still holds its recorded value, every finding is resolved with cited evidence and every retained assumption is named.
Replay the product proof sessions without saved heaps or databases, after installing the pinned Isabelle archive, AFP entry and formal foundation as the proof workflow does.
reproduction.passCriterion: Every declared session builds, and each proof audit export reports status PASS with oracle_dependency_count 0.

reproduction.purpose: For final frozen-source clean Assurance, rebuild every kernel session that the sealed kernel replay manifest names in a heap store and a system heap directory that both start empty, from the sealed sources only: the parent chain of the final target, including Pure and HOL from the pinned Isabelle distribution, and every further session whose recorded result a sealed record cites. The build uses the recorded catalog, options and process policy of the final chain, except that Pure, which has no parent heap, is built first without the process policy; the process policy is not a content option and enters no sources digest. No recorded heap, database or proof object is read; the recorded databases are only the comparison baseline.
reproduction.command: python3 EVIDENCE_ROOT/kernel-replay-kit-v1/tools/run_kernel_replay.py preflight --kit EVIDENCE_ROOT/kernel-replay-kit-v1 --run REPLAY_RUN_DIR --mode cold --root EVIDENCE=EVIDENCE_ROOT --root VERI=VERI_ROOT --root AFP=AFP_ENTRY; then powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File EVIDENCE_ROOT/kernel-replay-kit-v1/tools/start_detached.ps1 -Kit EVIDENCE_ROOT/kernel-replay-kit-v1 -Run REPLAY_RUN_DIR -Mode plan, and after a passing plan the same command with -Mode start; after the build exits, python3 EVIDENCE_ROOT/kernel-replay-kit-v1/tools/compare_kernel_replay.py --kit EVIDENCE_ROOT/kernel-replay-kit-v1 --run REPLAY_RUN_DIR. An interrupted build resumes in the same run directory and store with -Mode resume.
reproduction.passCriterion: The build plan in the empty store equals the sealed expected session list; the build exits 0 with every expected session finished and no other session built; every heap and database in the run store was created by this run; and for every expected session the comparison reports return code 0, no recorded error, the recorded sources digest, the recorded ancestor names, the recorded export inventory, the recorded theory exports and the recorded normalized messages, a database uuid that differs from the recorded one and no nonzero oracle count, with comparison status PASS_COLD_REPLAY_REPRODUCED.

reproduction.purpose: Recompute the recorded fingerprint of every expected session from its recorded database, after checking the database against the size and SHA-256 that the sealed manifest records, and compare it with the sealed baseline, so that the comparison baseline follows from the recorded results.
Regenerate every sealed input list from its recorded generator with the sealed tool, so that a file a recomputation newly reads, or no longer reads, is detected.
reproduction.command: For every list selector of the seal except the kernel replay kit list, which the kernel replay preflight checks file by file: python3 scripts/trust12/tail-preparation/assurance_inputs.py check --list EVIDENCE_ROOT/LIST_PATH --root PRODUCT=PRODUCT_CHECKOUT --root EVIDENCE=EVIDENCE_ROOT --root MAINTAINER=MAINTAINER_TOOLS --root VERI=VERI_ROOT --root AFP=AFP_ENTRY
reproduction.passCriterion: Status PASS_ASSURANCE_INPUT_LIST_REGENERATED for every sealed input list.

reproduction.purpose: Confirm that the inputs read by the Assurance are exactly the sealed inputs.
reproduction.command: python3 scripts/trust12/tail-preparation/assurance_seal.py verify --seal SEAL --root PRODUCT=PRODUCT_CHECKOUT --root EVIDENCE=EVIDENCE_ROOT --root MAINTAINER=MAINTAINER_TOOLS --root VERI=VERI_ROOT --root AFP=AFP_ENTRY
reproduction.passCriterion: Status PASS_ASSURANCE_INPUT_SEAL_VERIFIED before and after the Assurance run.

assuranceChecks.question: Can the command, state and receipt observables be reconstructed from the frozen schema, requirements and vectors alone, without reading the implementation?
procedure: Rebuild every conformance vector command, its calldata and its expected receipt from the kernel schema and the generated ABI only.
Rebuild the malformed input catalog from the kernel ABI and the generated bridge constants and compare it with the sealed catalog.
Compare the reconstruction with the sealed vectors and the sealed independent reproduction receipt.
assuranceChecks.passCriterion: Every reconstructed observable equals the sealed one.
assuranceChecks.onFailure: Return to Building. The assessor records the difference and never edits a sealed file.

assuranceChecks.question: Does every route, state write, event and theorem of the final artifacts belong to an obligation row or to a declared runtime-only item?
procedure: Enumerate every public and external selector of every profile runtime from a fresh build and compare it with the sealed route inventory.
Enumerate every storage variable and emitted event of the profile runtimes and compare them with the sealed state and receipt crosswalk.
Enumerate every ledger row and every cited theorem and report orphan theorems, orphan code, unmapped routes and unused lifecycle states.
assuranceChecks.passCriterion: No unmapped route, orphan state write, orphan theorem or unclassified selector remains.
assuranceChecks.onFailure: Return to Building with the list of orphans.

assuranceChecks.question: Does removing or weakening each load-bearing consumer actually break the claim that depends on it?
procedure: Replay every consumer-removal and certificate-removal negative that the runtime-link ledger cites: the kernel negatives are rebuilt by the cold kernel replay and compared session by session, and the negative outside the kernel is rechecked from its sealed record and the product mutation it is bound to.
Rerun the declared product mutation campaign on the sealed product checkout and require every declared mutation to be killed by its declared detector.

For each profile, rerun the malformed probe with one length guard disabled at a time, the word guard probe on every declared bounded word guard mutant, and the typed failure probe on every declared typed failure mutant, and require the declared outcome for each.
assuranceChecks.passCriterion: Every negative fails at the claimed consumer and at no earlier unrelated step.
assuranceChecks.onFailure: Return to Building with the surviving negative.

assuranceChecks.question: Do the numbers, hashes and statuses of the central closure artifact follow from the actual files, build exits and runtime outputs?
procedure: Rebuild the obligation ledger from the sealed evidence and compare every row status, count and hash.

Recompute the certificate registry from the sealed locator file and evidence, require it to equal the sealed registry byte for byte, and confirm that the public registry record, including the executed code of every certificate and the records that consumed every recorded world, follows from it.
Recompute the central closure counts and confirm that no row is closed by a human-written table alone.
assuranceChecks.passCriterion: Every recomputed number, hash and status equals the sealed artifact, and current mandatory rows are zero only if the recomputation says so.
assuranceChecks.onFailure: Return to Building. A mismatch is never resolved by editing the expected value.

reuse.policy: Final frozen-source clean Assurance reuses no kernel result: every runtime-link kernel session and every product proof session is rebuilt without recorded heaps or databases, and the recorded results serve only as the comparison baseline. The saved-mode recomputations read recorded prover outputs, such as stored proof graphs, compiled artifacts and forge reports, whose acceptance their checkpoints read rather than reprove; each such artifact is frozen by a sealed input list and must satisfy the five conditions below. A cache hit is never a check result.
conditions: Input identity: sources, transitive dependencies, generated inputs, statements and assumptions of the reused unit equal the sealed ones.
Tool identity: checker and compiler versions, dependency locks, build options and platform equal the sealed pins; Windows and Linux heaps are never exchanged.
Materialization: the reused heap, database, proof object or checked certificate is present and its recorded integrity hash matches.
Provenance: the producing repository, commit, run and permission of the reused state are recorded and trusted for the claim.
Current consumption: the native checker confirms freshness against the sealed sources and the final consumer reads the reused result.
coldReplayRequiredFor: an explicitly selected final frozen-source clean runtime-link replay
any release or final frozen-source clean Assurance claim
any toolchain or dependency pin change

exclusions: Conclusions, handoffs, status summaries and chat reports of the Building sessions are not Assurance inputs.
The assessor never edits a sealed file; any needed change returns the work to Building and requires a new seal.
A seal with status TEMPLATE_DRY_RUN is a format exercise and is never an Assurance input.
A participant of any Building session of this runtime link does not act as the independent assessor.
A seal produced from the current-completion specification is never relabeled or edited into a final seal.
The cold kernel replay never reads the recorded heap stores; their databases are opened read-only for the baseline check only.
